rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenants' Right to Know): just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot end a covered tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause and must state the cause in the notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must give 30/60 days' written notice, pay relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled) or waive that rent, and in some cases offer to re-rent within five years. Retaliation is barred and buyouts must follow disclosure and form rules.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation = 2 months' rent (3 for seniors/disabled)
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
City of San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause
rules.effective_date_note: Division retitled/amended by O-21647 N.S. (adopted 2023-05-25), effective 2023-06-24; later amendment O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28. Fact sheet (D077) also says June 24, 2023.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); mobilehomes under MRL; hotels/short-term; care facilities and transitional housing; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner; owner-occupied single-family or duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property owned by non-REIT/non-corporate landlord with written notice.
rules.penalty: Wrongful eviction damages of at least 3x actual economic damages; at least 3x unpaid relocation assistance plus actual damages; attorney's fees in court's discretion; punitive damages; non-compliant notice void; city enforcement.
rules.interaction: Consistent with and in addition to Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2; local rule governs where both apply.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable unit owned by non-corporate landlord with written notice
dormitories, care facilities, transitional housing, mobilehomes

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy levels, and no one may sell or license such software to a landlord. Tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees; each month and each property is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property
rules.effective_date_note: Official text (D076) is an unsigned draft taking effect on the 30th day after final passage; June 2025 comes from a law-firm alert (D002/D037), no day given.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data over 90 days old or public information without recommending rents, and software used to set rents/income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Civil action: injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

rules.review_note: Passage date not in the documents; enactment confirmed only by the secondary alert and litigation references.

no_rule_findings.finding: No San Diego local rent cap appears in the documents; the city's own tenant-protection notice points to the state cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12).
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information.

parsed.notes: Merged c70 and c110 (same Division 7) and c71, c88 and c101 (same Division 11). A San Diego source-of-income ordinance probably exists (link-only D075), but no provided document supports it, so I left it out. No documents cover security deposits, application fees or criminal-history screening at the city level.
